messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High latency SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming in prod-us-west-2. Alert: p99 > 4s for >= 5m. Paging maya (oncall).

maya: on it. ack. pulling graphs now. :rotating_light:

devon: confirming grafana shows p95 jumped from ~300ms to ~900ms and p99 near 5s. streaming.tail.stalls spiked 12x starting 08:06 UTC.

maya: any kv errors in logs? could be cache pressure or eviction storms.

ash: seeing a lot of kv.fetch latency and occasional timeouts. sample from node-7: `kv.fetch shard=us-west-2-s-3 keys=96 latency=2200ms` and `stream write stall detected node=node-7 seq=... duration=4.7s`.

devon: kube metrics show slab usage uneven across shards; some at ~94% used, some ~35%. pattern looks like rapid small-prefill bursts from a subset of customers.

ryan: customer impact: roughly 9% of streaming requests at p99, a couple of sessions observed client-side reconnects. Impacted customers concentrated in us-west-2 chat clusters. No global degradation.

maya: quick mitigations to try: 1) reduce prefill concurrency in us-west-2, 2) increase per-shard eviction aggressiveness, 3) short-lived traffic spill to us-east-1 for heavy streamers, 4) selective restart of highly-fragmented nodes if evictions don't help.

ash: i can scale prefill down and bump eviction params. commands ready:
```
# scale prefill workers down in us-west-2
kubectl -n serving-scale scale deploy/prefill-workers --replicas=1 --context=prod-us-west-2

# tweak eviction threshold
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" -d '{"kv.evict_target_pct": 78, "kv.evict_batch_size": 48}'
```

devon: i can kick a 15% spill to us-east-1 via routing patch. will monitor latency rollups.

maya: ash, do the prefill scale and eviction change. devon, start 15% spill. ryan, prepare a short internal customer note after we confirm improvement.

ash: prefill workers scaled to 1 replica. eviction params updated (kv.evict_batch_size=48, kv.evict_target_pct=78).

ops-bot: routing patch rollout started: 2/5 nodes updated.

devon: spill applied at 15% — p99 dropped from ~5s -> ~2.3s over ~3 minutes, p95 trending to ~480ms. streaming.tail.stalls metric down ~60%.

maya: good signal. ash, any sign of eviction thrash or oscillation?

ash: eviction rate increased ~2.8x on hot shards; freed bytes up ~22% on the most impacted shard. no eviction-loop patterns so far. kv.fetch timeout logs decreased significantly.

ryan: customer impact now ~2% p99. drafting internal update: brief summary + mitigation steps + next steps. will post to #customer-success in 20m.

maya: next steps and owners:
- ash: keep watching slab free bytes and eviction effectiveness. if free bytes decline again for >10m, prepare node restart for top fragmented nodes.
- devon: hold spill at 15% for 10m, if stable consider bump to 25%.
- maya: collect slab dump from node-7 and start root cause notes.

ash: running slab dump: `kv-slab-dump --shard us-west-2-s-3 --out /tmp/slab-node-7.json && gzip /tmp/slab-node-7.json && scp ops-server:/slabs/2026-03-15-node-7.gz`

devon: monitoring update 8m post-mitigation: p99=1.8s, p95=430ms, streaming.tail.stalls down 72%.

maya: marking incident mitigated in tracker but keeping the channel open for handoff and postmortem. creating follow-up ticket for fragmentation analysis and prefill backpressure improvements.

pagerduty-bot: INC-20260315-89 mitigated by maya. Follow-up task created: T-9812 (kv-cache fragmentation analysis & prefill throttling).

ryan: posted customer-safe message to #customer-success: "We've observed intermittent high tail latency in us-west-2 due to internal KV cache pressure; we've mitigated by throttling prefill work and routing a portion of traffic to a healthy region. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

jamie: taking 12:00 handoff. will watch p99 and streaming.tail.stalls. please attach slab dump link to incident doc.

maya: slab dump uploaded: https://ops-storage.internal/slabs/2026-03-15-node-7-slab.gz. handoff to @jamie: things stable but continue to monitor for regression.

ash: added logs and eviction metrics to incident artifact bucket.

maya: tidy follow-ups: investigate prefill bursts correlation to customer traffic, add adaptive per-shard eviction thresholds, add earlier backpressure in prefill pipeline, verify no recent deploys affected allocation logic.

jamie: ack. taking over monitoring and postmortem coordination.

maya: thanks all. closing live mitigation thread. great coordination. :clap:
